records.verificationNote: Fetched member.carefirst.com/carefirst-resources/pdf/exchange-formulary-sum7277-2026.pdf via curl and parsed locally with pypdf (plain WebFetch returned only unparsed binary PDF stream data). Page 1 confirms 'CareFirst Exchange Formulary 2026 ... Last updated 06/01/26'. Pages 43-44 (in-document numbering), under CARDIOVASCULAR > ACE INHIBITORS (and the preceding ACE INHIBITOR COMBINATIONS subsection), list verbatim every one of benazepril, captopril, enalapril, fosinopril, lisinopril, moexipril, perindopril, quinapril, ramipril, and trandolapril as Tier 1 with a completely blank Requirements/Limits column for every single strength -- meaning no PA, ST, or QL applies to any ACE inhibitor monotherapy or combination product in this formulary. Selected lisinopril 10mg as the preferred agent per national first-line guideline convention, since the document itself applies no differential restriction among any of the nine molecules -- all are equally 'preferred, no PA' and captured as alternatives. Confirmed by full-document case-insensitive search that no brand name (Zestril, Prinivil, Vasotec, Lotensin, Altace, Accupril, Monopril, Univasc, Aceon, Mavik, Capoten) appears anywhere in the 235-page text -- this class is completely generic-substituted with zero brand presence, and there is no drug in this class that fails to appear on the formulary (unlike SABA/ICS/ICS-LABA/LAMA, every common ACE inhibitor generic is present), so paRequired is empty. No class-wide step-therapy or BOGL language found near this section. [Reused 2026-10-21 for DC: same document as the MD guide (the CareFirst exchange formulary and the Kaiser Mid-Atlantic marketplace formulary cover DC, MD and VA).]

preferredAgent.plainSig: Take 1 tablet by mouth once a day

records.verificationNote: Read from page 18 ('caption continues from ACE inhibitor / ARB section') of the KP Mid-Atlantic Marketplace Formulary, last update 04/07/2026: 'lisinopril 1' and 'lisinopril & hydrochlorothiazide 1' at Tier 1 with no PA/ST flag. Same page lists 'captopril 1', 'enalapril maleate 1, 3', 'quinapril hcl 3', 'ramipril 3' — all covered with no PA/ST/nonformulary flags, so classified as alternatives at varying tiers rather than rejects. No ACE inhibitor in this section carries a PA or step-therapy marker per the document's own key. [Reused 2026-10-21 for DC: same document as the MD guide (the CareFirst exchange formulary and the Kaiser Mid-Atlantic marketplace formulary cover DC, MD and VA).]
